---
title: "Project cohorts and simulate patients"
description: "Choose starting profiles, inspect occupancy and update patient covariates during simulation."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
invisible(capture.output(source(system.file(
  "examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"
), local = TRUE)))
```

Use `projectCohort()` for expected occupancy of a fixed cohort. Use
`simulateTrajectories()` when individual states, eligibility or covariates must
be updated. Both use supplied probabilities; neither estimates new models.

Examples use the [quickstart objects](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/quickstart.R).
Load them in a new R session with:

```{r load-example, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"))
```

## Project a fixed starting distribution

```{r project}
projection <- projectCohort(
  transitions, nCycles = 4, initial = c(Stable = 1), cohortSize = 100
)
head(projection$occupancy, 6)
transitionMatrix(projection, cycle = 0)
```

Four steps produce five distributions: the initial label and four subsequent
labels. Expected counts can be fractional. Each step selects the matrix using
the source cycle's elapsed day. The final period remains in use for the requested
horizon; an infinite period does not establish empirical lifetime validity.

Without `initial` or `entry`, projection uses the fitted `entryCounts` first-label
mix. A named `initial` vector supplies first-label probabilities; omitted known
states receive zero. Supplied stage models need an explicit start or entry model.
For a stratified fit, select one element of `models` to project that group.

An unavailable row is harmless while its state has zero mass. If a step needs
that row, projection stops. `flows` distinguishes conditional probabilities
from the whole cohort's probability mass. Absorbing self-transitions retain
occupancy; they are not new deaths. Ordered models also retain `stageFlows`.

## Apply entry once, when needed

```{r project-entry}
entry <- estimateEntryTransitions(histories, entryState = "Stable")
from_entry <- projectCohort(transitions, nCycles = 3, entry = entry, cohortSize = 100)
from_entry$entry$baseline_distribution
```

In `projectCohort()`, non-`NULL` `initial` and `entry` are mutually exclusive.
Entry uses its eligible baseline mix to generate the first label at cycle zero.
It adds no timepoint, baseline living time or recurring baseline charge.
`nCycles = 0` applies entry alone. Three subsequent steps produce labels 0–3.
A manually calculated first-label mix can reproduce occupancy through `initial`,
while an entry model also retains baseline-to-outcome flows and entry effects.

## Simulate explicit patients or distributions

```{r simulate}
bundle <- createModelBundle(transitions)
simulation <- simulateTrajectories(
  bundle, n = 100, initial = c(Stable = 1), nSteps = 4,
  terminalStates = "Dead", seed = 42
)
head(simulation$population, 3)
```

A bundle stores models and grouping rules, without a training population.
For stratified simulation, supply a `population` with one snapshot per patient
and the required covariates. Optional `subject_id` must be unique. Omit `n` to
use every profile once; `n` and `replace = TRUE` sample profiles with replacement.
`simulation_id` identifies each draw and `source_subject_id` records its source.

A named `initial` vector replaces sampled states independently of covariates.
Without a population, stratified models need a joint `initial` table containing
`state_label`, `probability` and covariates. All supplied positive-probability
starting profiles must have support, including profiles not eventually drawn.

Simulation can combine `entry` with explicit baseline profiles or `initial`;
it does not adopt the entry estimator's training population or baseline mix.
Entry requires zero starting clocks, runs once before the initial snapshot,
and does not call `updateCovariates`. Stratified entry selects baseline groups
once; later transition grouping remains dynamic. See the
[entry example](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/entry-simulation.R).

## Advance time and update covariates

`elapsed_day` and `cycle` default to zero. Days must align with the cycle length.
A step selects the source model, draws the state, advances time, updates
nonterminal covariates, then recomputes groups for the next draw.

With `birth_date` and `index_date` Date columns, age is completed calendar years
at `index_date + elapsed_day`. Numeric age alone changes only through a callback:

```{r update-age}
profiles <- data.frame(subject_id = "example", state_label = "Stable", age = 64.99)
age_run <- simulateTrajectories(
  bundle, population = profiles, nSteps = 2, terminalStates = "Dead", seed = 42,
  updateCovariates = function(current, previous) data.frame(
    simulation_id = current$simulation_id,
    age = previous$age + (current$elapsed_day - previous$elapsed_day) / 365.25
  )
)
age_run$population[c("simulation_id", "elapsed_day", "age")]
```

Callbacks return `simulation_id` plus changed raw covariates. IDs, states, clocks,
age-defining dates and derived groups are protected. Use the same grouping rules
before fitting and in the bundle. A final destination may have no matching
model, but the next draw from it fails; there is no pooled fallback.

## Inspect and resume a run

`trajectories` stores labelled snapshots, `transitions` stores actual draws,
and `population` stores the latest snapshot. Ordered draws also populate
`stageTransitions`. Terminal covariates stay fixed while other patients continue.

```{r resume}
continued <- advanceSimulation(simulation, nSteps = 2)
continued$metadata$steps
```

Resume retains rules, charged-component memory and the private RNG checkpoint.
The last snapshot is not charged twice. Split runs match uninterrupted runs when
callbacks depend on their arguments and saved configuration. Terminal or custom
stopping remains final. Supply an explicit seed for reproducible initialization.

For observed occupancy, use `summariseOccupancy()` and inspect `coverage`.
`compareOccupancy()` is descriptive: its observed available-state denominator
can shrink, while projection keeps a fixed cohort. Continue to
[economic accounting](costs-and-economic-outcomes.html).
